clue.text: It's no advantage to retire

definitions.meaning: a handicap or disadvantage, the opposite of a benefit
to withdraw or pull away, as troops pull back from a position

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that stepping down from work brings no benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage is a handicap, and to withdraw is to pull back from a place; the two-word phrase and the single word cover both senses.

clue.text: A drop of water to drink — it goes down the throat

parts.note: dew is drops of water that form overnight
to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: A drink of water slipping down someone's gullet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes down the throat' suggests swallowing, but it describes a fold of skin that hangs down from the neck, as on cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the loose fold of skin hanging from the neck of cattle or other animals, below the chin.

clue.text: Ring up soldiers in army rising plot

indicators.note: in places the bell and soldier pieces inside the army word
rising, in a down clue, means the army word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the ringing word is read upwards

parts.note: to toll is to ring a bell
men are soldiers, the other ranks

explanation.surface: A phone call warns soldiers about a plot hatched among rising troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' and 'rising' each turn their own piece, as down clues read upwards. In Britain an allotment is a small rented plot for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of land rented out by a council for growing vegetables is a typically British gardening patch.

clue.text: A sort of quiz in worker's game

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the insect word

parts.note: a worker bee is the stock crossword worker

indicators.note: a sort of suggests a variant version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of quiz forms part of an employee's pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sort of' rearranges the quiz letters into ZIQU. The worker is the bee, the stock crossword worker. Bezique is a card game for two players.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a card game for two players using a double pack, popular in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Leave fish without a tail

indicators.note: without a tail means the fish word loses its final letter

parts.note: a conger is a large sea eel, a fish

explanation.surface: Instructions to leave a fish with its tail cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like an instruction but is a noun: a congé is permission to depart, or a dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: From French, the word means formal permission to depart, or a dismissal, as leave can.

clue.text: Concord moving in on us

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the words that follow are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Agreement shifting in our favour, as if a treaty were being negotiated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges INONUS, the letters of 'in on us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Concord is harmony or agreement, and acting all together in agreement is acting as one voice.

clue.text: A number object to love

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A figure of speech: some number objects to romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a verb (to protest) but is the noun. In tennis scoring 'love' means zero.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring love means a score of zero, which is nil or nought.

clue.text: Divide 50 into what you dig

indicators.note: into means the numeral goes inside the digging word

parts.note: a spit is a spade's depth of earth, what a gardener digs
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A gardener divides fifty plants into the bed being dug.
explanation.walkthrough: A SPIT is the depth of one spade's blade, a gardening term.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate something into parts is to cleave or break it apart.

clue.text: Japanese coppers turn up around composer's vicinity

indicators.note: around tells us the reversed coins go around the composer piece
turn up, in a down clue, means the coin word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the sen was a small Japanese coin, a hundredth of a yen
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia; the possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: Japanese police arrive near a composer's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police but means small coins; 'turn up' makes NES, which wraps round the composer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeness or proximity to a place is the state of being in its neighbourhood.

clue.text: Runner more complacent about start of lap

indicators.note: about means the comparative word goes round the single letter

parts.note: smugger means more self-satisfied

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An athlete grows more self-satisfied at the start of a lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete on a track, but means someone who runs goods past customs.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun-runner or rum-runner carries contraband illegally across borders, the trade of a smuggler.

clue.text: Antipodean dancing girl

parts.note: read literally, a girl from Australia called Matilda who is doing a ballroom dance in triple time

explanation.surface: An Australian girl on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous Australian bush ballad takes its title from slang for tramping with a swag, but the clue reads the title literally as a girl doing a ballroom dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The unofficial Australian anthem's title, read literally, describes a girl named Matilda performing a ballroom dance.

clue.text: It's old-fashioned — being against what the French say

parts.note: anti means opposed to or against
que is the French word for 'what'

explanation.surface: Someone is called behind the times for opposing French ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Something antiquated or from an earlier era is out of date and belongs to the past.

clue.text: Cast a little light on one way through the valley

indicators.note: the valley word runs through, i.e. surrounds, the letters for one and way

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland
I is the Roman numeral for one
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone shines a faint lamp along a path through a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine faintly or sparkle is to give off a small amount of light.

clue.text: Is Leeds apt to make a stand?

indicators.note: to make signals that the letters of the preceding words are reworked to form something new

explanation.surface: A question whether the city of Leeds is ready to make a stand on some issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges LEEDSAPT, the letters of 'Leeds apt'. LEEDS is a city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth or base on which a statue or vase is placed is a stand for it.

clue.text: Decrepit wrist-watch?

definitions.meaning: worn out and shabby with age
a wrist-watch is a timepiece carried on the arm, read literally as two words

explanation.surface: Someone describes their old wrist-watch as falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shabby with age is worn out by the years; and a wrist-watch is a timepiece someone wears.

clue.text: German physicist admits us to energy source

indicators.note: admits means the fuel word lets the other piece inside it

parts.note: gas is a fuel, a source of energy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A German scientist lets us in on a source of power.
explanation.walkthrough: Carl Friedrich GAUSS was a German mathematician and physicist; the unit of magnetic flux density is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Friedrich Gauss was a celebrated German mathematician and physicist who studied magnetism.

clue.text: Found out such appliances are dangerous

definitions.meaning: electrical appliances lacking a ground connection are unsafe

explanation.surface: A safety warning that certain discovered appliances are hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as un-earthed: an electrical appliance without an earth (US: ground) wire is unsafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something discovered has been dug up, and electrical equipment with no ground wire lacks earthing.

clue.text: Renegade — a petty officer, say

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for petty officer, a naval rank
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A deserter is identified as a naval petty officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat who abandons their faith or party is a renegade.

clue.text: Bowl is smaller than jug

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to bowl is to deliver the ball to the batsman
a jug is a pitcher, and this word is that one cut short, so it is smaller

explanation.surface: A comparison of kitchen vessels: the bowl is the smaller of the two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' looks like a kitchen dish but is the cricket verb, to deliver the ball. The second half is cryptic: the answer is 'pitcher' (a jug) minus its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball and cricket, delivering the ball is throwing it; and a pitcher is a jug, of which the answer is a shorter piece.

clue.text: Gather in ' broken hearts; about five

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the numeral
broken says the letters of the word that follows are smashed into a new order

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Collecting broken hearts, around five of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges HEARTS into HAREST, which goes around V.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap a crop is to collect it from the fields at the end of the season.

clue.text: One who shifts, around mineral aggregate too.

indicators.note: around tells us the word for one who shifts goes around the mineral word

parts.note: a mover is someone who shifts things, for example a removal man
ore is rock from which a metal is extracted, a mineral aggregate

explanation.surface: A removal worker is described standing among heaps of minerals as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The mineral goes in right after the mover's first letter; 'too' is the definition, meaning 'besides'.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and besides both mean in addition, the sense of this word.

clue.text: Pampered sort of deer, prime bit of venison

indicators.note: sort is read as a verb, to sort or reorder the letters that follow
prime bit of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A kind of deer and a choice cut of venison, eaten by someone spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like a noun in 'sort of deer' but rearranges OF, DEER and V (the first letter of venison).
explanation.definitionFit: Indulged with too much food, someone pampered has been given more than enough to eat.

clue.text: Writer hear his work

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
to try a case is to hear it in court

explanation.surface: Someone is told to listen to an author's latest work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hear' is the judge's verb: to hear a case is to try it.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is the creative output of a writer like Poe, so it is his work.

clue.text: Fight — brawl — ''caused Robin's death

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do in practice
a row is a noisy quarrel or brawl

explanation.surface: A fight and a brawl led to the death of someone called Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme 'Who Killed Cock Robin?', the sparrow says 'I, with my bow and arrow' killed him; the definition reads as 'what caused Robin's death'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old English nursery rhyme the small brown bird confesses to killing Cock Robin with an arrow.

clue.text: Beam — not right ahead, more towards the stern

indicators.note: not means the right letter is taken away from the beam word
ahead places the removed letter at the front of the beam word

parts.note: a rafter is a sloping roof beam

explanation.surface: A nautical instruction about a beam, positions ahead and towards the stern of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' and 'ahead' sound nautical, but 'Beam' is a roof timber; on a ship, aft is towards the stern, so this is further back.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship aft means towards the back, and this word is a nautical comparative form meaning further back.

clue.text: Valediction to gladden Number Ten

parts.note: to cheer someone is to gladden them
IO looks like the digits 1 and 0, which make ten

explanation.surface: A farewell speech meant to lift spirits at Downing Street, the Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number Ten' suggests 10 Downing Street, the British Prime Minister's home, but it gives IO, letters shaped like 1 and 0.
explanation.definitionFit: A valediction is a farewell, and this informal British word is a way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Many works out east, whence comes oil

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

indicators.note: out means the compass letter is taken out of the musical works

parts.note: an opera is a musical work, and opera is also the plural of opus, works

explanation.surface: Lots of factories in the east, where oil is produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' suggests factories, but it is OPERA (plural of opus).
explanation.definitionFit: Dried coconut kernel is the source from which coconut oil is pressed.

clue.text: For a poet, that had changed without delay

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the preceding words are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A poet has altered something and done so promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges FORAPOETTHATHAD, the letters of 'For a poet' and 'that had'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly or at the slightest signal, as if starting when a hat falls.

clue.text: Desert, in time, slips

indicators.note: in says the deserting word sits inside the word for a period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
to rat is to desert or betray one's side

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a post and has lapses along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slips' looks like a verb but is a noun: slips are mistakes, and the answer is a list of printing mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are small mistakes, and this Latin plural names mistakes in a printed book.

clue.text: In truth, I had left sweet outside

indicators.note: outside means the sweet word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: candy is a sweet, especially in American English
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone admits honestly that they left a sweet outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking frankly and honestly is speaking with sincerity, which is what in truth conveys.
